### 6.1 Identical re-key matcher (final critic F-M07; owner R-101; precedence over R-112)

**Why.** A roster row's work-event identity is its Request Id (`identity_kind='PROFILE_EXTERNAL_KEY'`; key lookup in `public.weekly_source_upload_context_v1`, `08102026_1635_weekly_source_released_client_eligibility_v1.sql:409-428`; event creation in `public.weekly_source_projection_rows_apply_atomic_v1`, controlling definition `07102026_2215_weekly_source_same_file_recheck_recovery_v1.sql`). A re-keyed shift is therefore a new work event; with Q-N3 keeping the old one as paid, an ADD would pay the worker twice.

1. **Match rule.** For a finalised export row whose Request Id has no work event in its group and profile, look for work events of the same group and profile (`PROFILE_EXTERNAL_KEY`) whose latest RESOLVED resolution has the **same Candidate, client, Contract, work date, start, end and break**, and whose own Request Id is **absent** from this upload although the upload's confirmed coverage includes that date. Exactly one → that event is the row's `prior_work_event_id`. None → a new work event (today's path). More than one → no suggestion (item 4).
2. **Where.** New private helper `private.weekly_source_identical_rekey_prior_v1(p_upload_row_id uuid) returns uuid` (owner `postgres`; `service_role` EXECUTE revoked; called only by `SECURITY DEFINER` owners). A later successor of `public.weekly_source_upload_context_v1` calls it when the key lookup at `:409-428` finds nothing. A later successor of `public.weekly_source_projection_rows_apply_atomic_v1` **re-proves** it: for a `PROFILE_EXTERNAL_KEY` row whose key has no event, a Worker-supplied `prior_work_event_id` must equal the helper's answer, else `WEEKLY_SOURCE_REKEY_MATCH_UNPROVEN`. The existing prior-event branch then reuses the old event (`07102026_2215…:580-600`; match kind `EXACT_DURABLE_LINEAGE`, so the closed lists at `plan6:600` and `:979` are unchanged) and the `DURABLE_LINEAGE` selection re-proves the same Contract (`:364-399`). Confirm both controlling definitions at WP-0. The match recomputes identically on every later import (the old Id stays absent; the new Id never gets its own event).
3. **Effect.** The transition is NO_CHANGE (WP-F2 compares values), so pay is unchanged — paid once. The old Id is **not** listed "Not in the latest file · kept as paid" (I-12), because its work event is present. Invoice: **report membership (Acacium)** — the new report line binds by its Request Id to the export row and through it to the old work event; it is invoiced on its report as the Trust billed it, amber "! No hold · Billed again by the Trust · also on report DD/MM/YYYY". **Window membership (Surrey, Magnit-style)** — when the re-keyed row falls inside this cycle's window and its work event was invoiced in an earlier cycle, the cycle finalisation writes one invoice-only movement `source_line_kind='SOURCE_REBILL_LINE'` through new owner `private.weekly_source_rebill_movement_insert_v1`: the revision's own profile kind, `movement_role='POSITIVE'`, origin = that NO_CHANGE transition's `transition_id` (free, because NO_CHANGE writes no movement; unique `(transition_id, movement_role)`, `plan6:1139-1141`), pay vector zero, charge and VAT from the row as for any line, excluded from pay by line kind (§19.2). So the invoice still equals the Trust's run (owner round 2: both lines stay invoiced). NEXT's transition capture uses the prior snapshot's movement for NO_CHANGE and never reads movements by transition for it (`04102026_0475…:313-345`). Re-keys were seen only for Whittington (10/10, HELPER_C C5); the window case is proved on a synthetic row (RK-4).
4. **Every other overlap with an already-paid shift** (old Id still present, or any value different) is the NHSP-pack Q14 blocked row *Separate shift / Same shift (already billed)* (R-115), through the NHSP pack's new blocker `PAID_SHIFT_OVERLAP_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` and its row choice `pay_effect` (NHSP `03_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md:235-240`). The existing `office_selected_work_event_id` / `office_separate_shift` path (`broker/src/weekly-source/upload-publication-owner.mjs:449-459`) lists **protected** shifts only (`private.weekly_source_protected_match_candidates_v1`, `01102026_1201_weekly_source_combined_workspace.sql:454-489`), so it cannot raise this row for an unprotected paid shift (confirmation critic). Q-N3's kept-as-paid default no longer supplies the CANCEL the NHSP extension relied on, so this row is the route (RK-3).
5. **NEXT:** one payable position per work event; handoff NX-8 asks Banking Pay to confirm (X-11).

Tests: G-3, I-12, RK-1…RK-4, X-11 (`05`).

The folded NHSP package is, by name: **WP-R1, WP-R2 (reversal tuple and pinning to the original Contract, NHSP `03_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md:68-85`), WP-R2b (Q9: a replacement on the original Contract is valued at its original pay card/channel, NEXT resolving rates under its own rules, `:87-114`; no new frozen-rate policy is invented), WP-R3–R8, WP-R9(c) (Q14 *Separate shift / Same shift (already billed)*: Same is invoice-only with `pay_effect='NONE'` and absent from active pay; Separate creates a distinct event; `:235-239`), WP-R12–R14**, plus D1 (invoice admission preservation) and K12 (deliberate Timesheet placement). `pay_effect='NONE'` ships in the **same** controlling successor of `active_movements_v1` as §19.2. **Override oracles** (later main rulings win): NHSP K4 (Contract start moved to Monday) is replaced by CN-1 (earliest actual worked day, R-110); NHSP H2 (already-paid absent line cancelled with invoice reversal) is replaced by G-4 / G-4c / KP-1 (R-112, R-173); NHSP H5 (conditional NET move) is replaced by N5-1 (two lines, R-114). NH-1 is an exact selector (`05` §14).

scope: Same work already paid versus separate Source work; not SAME_TIMESHEET Contract correction or Contract A-to-B mode.
